question_record.context: A security incident involving the Mimikatz credential theft tool was detected on the device `vnevado-win10v` on 2024-07-04. Mimikatz is used by attackers to harvest credentials such as plaintext passwords, password hashes, smartcard PINs, and Kerberos tickets. The presence of the Mimikatz tool indicates that an attacker might be attempting to log into this or other devices on the network by impersonating a valid user.
question_record.question: Who was the user account that had a Security Identification (SID) history injection detected in this incident?
solution: The credential theft tool Mimikatz was detected being executed by `powershell.exe`.
There was a Security Identification (SID) history injection detected involving the account `lucasb`.

108.name: Mimikatz credential theft tool
108.description:
The Mimikatz hacktool was detected on this device. Mimikatz is a credential theft tool that can harvest plaintext passwords, password hashes, smartcard PINs, and Kerberos tickets.  An attacker might be trying to harvest credentials to log into this or other devices on the network, by impersonating a valid user.

For more information, read the Mimikatz tool profile Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/51db19ab-081f-46f3-9fe1-3f5e5d2f8ee0/analystreport? and read the Actor profile: Storm-0875 Threat Analytics report https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/4f60801d-912e-4bcb-91b2-f46879c8a718/analystreport

93.name: SID history injection
93.description: A Security IDentifcation (SID) history injection was detected on this device. SID history is an attribute that supports migration scenarios. Attackers typically use attack tools to change the SID history of an existing domain user to an SID with elevated privileges. With elevated privileges, the affected process might be able to access sensitive files, ensure persistence, and modify system settings.
